Summary Lim Guan Eng urged Indonesia to compensate Malaysia for haze losses or form a task force for firefighting in Indonesian forests.
 Lim cited economic losses of up to RM13 billion in Malaysia due to health impacts and tourism decline from the haze.
 He proposed a RM1,000 tax rebate for air purifiers and called for a permanent ASEAN haze relief task force to address recurring haze issues.
 Make Malay Mail your preferred source on Google Giving you news that matter to Malaysians. Make Malay Mail your preferred source when you search for news on Google. By Malay Mail First Published: Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 10:17 AM MYT × Subscribe to Newsletter
 Subscribe KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has urged Indonesia to either compensate Malaysia for losses arising from this year’s haze crisis or agree to the formation of a permanent trans-boundary firefighting task force with the authority to enter Indonesian forests immediately to combat fires.
 In a statement today, Lim said Malaysia should accept the apology offered by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to Malaysia and Singapore over the prolonged haze episode in the spirit of good neighbourly relations and ASEAN solidarity.
 However, he said Indonesia could not disclaim responsibility for the duration and impact of the crisis, which he said had been worsened by this year’s Super El Nino conditions.
 Lim claimed that Malaysia had suffered welfare losses of RM8 billion linked to health impacts and economic losses of RM5 billion as a result of the haze.
 He cited a study commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers, which estimated that severe air pollution could reduce international tourist arrivals by up to eight per cent and jeopardise the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign, with potential losses of up to RM5 billion in tourism-related gross domestic product.
 According to Lim, the estimated RM8 billion in welfare losses reflected the economic cost associated with premature mortality risks and was linked to an estimated 1,700 premature deaths among Malaysians.
 He said measures such as the use of air purifiers were essential during severe haze episodes and reiterated his earlier proposal for a RM1,000 tax rebate for the purchase of air purifiers to help protect vulnerable groups, particularly young children and senior citizens.
 Lim said that if Indonesia was unable to provide compensation, it should agree to the establishment of a Permanent Trans-Boundary Haze Relief Task Force comprising trained personnel capable of undertaking immediate firefighting operations in Indonesian forests.
 He said such a mechanism was necessary to prevent haze from becoming a recurring annual disaster in the region.
 The former finance minister also called on Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to formally convey the proposal to Indonesia, arguing that a standing regional firefighting force with rapid deployment powers would enable ASEAN to respond more effectively to forest fires and trans-boundary haze incidents.
 He added that concerns over national sovereignty should not stand in the way of practical solutions to address a problem that continues to affect millions of people across the region.
